arxiv-2102-12594.title: Directional Bias Amplification
arxiv-2102-12594.creator: Angelina Wang and Olga Russakovsky
arxiv-2102-12594.description: Abstract Mitigating bias in machine learning systems requires refining our understanding of bias propagation pathways: from societal structures to large-scale data to trained models to impact on society. In this work, we focus on one aspect of the problem, namely bias amplification : the tendency of models to amplify the biases present in the data they are trained on.

arxiv-2111-05301.title: Adaptable Register File Organization for Vector Processors
arxiv-2111-05301.creator: Cristóbal Ramírez Lazo, Enrico Reggiani, Carlos Rojas Morales, Roger Figueras Bagué, Luis Alfonso Villa Vargas, Marco Antonio Ramírez Salinas, Mateo Valero Cortés, Osman Sabri Ünsal, Adrián Cristal
arxiv-2111-05301.description: Abstract Modern scientific applications are getting more diverse, and the vector lengths in those applications vary widely. arxiv-2202-10450.title: A Survey of Ad Hoc Teamwork Research
arxiv-2202-10450.creator: Reuth Mirsky, Ignacio Carlucho, Arrasy Rahman, Elliot Fosong, William Macke, Mohan Sridharan, Peter Stone, Stefano V. Albrecht
arxiv-2202-10450.description: Abstract Ad hoc teamwork is the research problem of designing agents that can collaborate with new teammates without prior coordination. This survey makes a two-fold contribution: First, it provides a structured description of the different facets of the ad hoc teamwork problem.

arxiv-2411-06648.title: Driven Critical Dynamics in Measurement-induced Phase Transitions
arxiv-2411-06648.creator: Wantao Wang, Shuo Liu, Jiaqiang Li, Shi-Xin Zhang, Shuai Yin
arxiv-2411-06648.description: Abstract Measurement-induced phase transitions (MIPT), characterizing abrupt changes in entanglement properties in quantum many-body systems subjected to unitary evolution with interspersed projective measurements, have garnered increasing interest. In this work, we generalize the Kibble-Zurek (KZ) driven critical dynamics that has achieved great success in traditional quantum and classical phase transitions to MIPT.

arxiv-2506-18448.title: GraspMAS: Zero-Shot Language-driven Grasp Detection with Multi-Agent System
arxiv-2506-18448.creator: Quang Nguyen, Tri Le, Huy Nguyen, Thieu Vo, Tung Ta, Baoru Huang, Minh Vu, Anh Nguyen
arxiv-2506-18448.description: Abstract Language-driven grasp detection has the potential to revolutionize human-robot interaction by allowing robots to understand and execute grasping tasks based on natural language commands. However, existing approaches face two key challenges. First, they often struggle to interpret complex text instructions or operate ineffectively in densely cluttered environments.

arxiv-2511-04382.title: Lattice design of a storage-ring-based light source for generating high-power fully coherent EUV radiation
arxiv-2511-04382.creator: Yu-Jie Lu, Ao Liu, Chang-liang Li, Kun Wang, Qing-lei Zhang, Wei-shi Wan, Wei-jie Fan, Jun-hao Liu, Rui-chun Li, Yan-xu Wang, Kong-long Wu, Ji Li, Chao Feng
arxiv-2511-04382.description: Abstract We present the physical design and systematic optimization of a high-performance storage ring tailored for the generation of high-power coherent radiation, with particular emphasis on the extreme ultraviolet (EUV) regime. The proposed ring adopts a Double Bend Achromat (DBA) lattice configuration and integrates 12 superconducting wigglers to significantly enhance radiation damping and minimize the natural emittance.

pmc-11509472.title: Erosive Tarsal Conjunctival Lesions Following Immunogenic Events in Early Development of Ocular Graft-vs-Host Disease
pmc-11509472.creator: Marcus G Kohnstam, Pier Luigi Surico, Zhonghui K Luo, Alba Martín-Gil, Laura De Diego-García
pmc-11509472.description: Purpose: Ocular graft-versus-host disease (oGVHD) affects more than half of the patients following allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). The disease onset and the pathogenesis of oGVHD are not well understood. We hope to identify the triggers and explore the clinical signs and symptoms of oGVHD development at the early stages.

pmc-12570938.title: Host perceptions of an undergraduate semester abroad: strengthening partnerships in global health education
pmc-12570938.creator: Myriam Vuckovic, Joseph Mulinge, Stephen Ledet, Margaret Baker
pmc-12570938.description: AbstractObjectivesAs global health education becomes more embedded in university curricula, the availability of experiential learning opportunities in this field has expanded as well. These programmes offer students valuable exposure to diverse cultural perspectives and help develop essential competencies in global health.

pmc-12588920.title: Global trends and health system impact on polycystic ovary syndrome: a comprehensive analysis of age-stratified females from 1990 to 2021
pmc-12588920.creator: Weiwei Zeng, Dali Gan, Juanfeng Ou, Brian Tomlinson
pmc-12588920.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a major factor in female infertility. The global burden of PCOS has generally been neglected due to insufficient data. This study aims to comprehensively assess the burden of PCOS among females aged 10–54 years globally from 1990 to 2021, to project trends for the next two decades, and to evaluate the impact of health system levels on PCOS prevalence.

pmc-12639796.title: Recurrent acute necrotizing pancreatitis secondary to hypercalcemic crisis in hyperparathyroidism: a case report
pmc-12639796.creator: Kun Zou, Tianbin Cai, Rui Liu, Junqiang Zhang
pmc-12639796.description: BackgroundAlthough less common, metabolic disorders such as hypercalcemia are implicated in the pathogenesis of acute pancreatitis. Persistent hypercalcemia may lead to recurrent acute pancreatitis if the underlying etiology remains untreated.Case presentationA 56-year-old Chinese female patient with a history of hypercalcemia-associated acute pancreatitis 3 years earlier presented with recurrent acute necrotizing pancreatitis lasting for 4 weeks.

pmc-12654674.title: Marine Natural Products in Preclinical Cancer Studies: Ten Years of Advanced Total Synthesis
pmc-12654674.creator: Ester Colarusso, Assunta Giordano, Maria Giovanna Chini, Giuseppe Bifulco, Gianluigi Lauro, Naoyuki Kotoku, Haruhiko Fuwa
pmc-12654674.description: Marine ecosystems represent an exceptional reservoir of structurally diverse metabolites with remarkable pharmacological potential. Over the past decades, the exploration of marine organisms has led to the discovery of an ever-expanding number of bioactive compounds. Many of these metabolites display highly original chemical scaffolds that are not typically found in terrestrial organisms, offering new opportunities for drug discovery.

pmc-13094909.title: When care demands rise: Exploring the impact of hemiparesis dependency and healthcare challenges among caregivers at a tertiary hospital in Bhubaneswar
pmc-13094909.creator: Samapika Rout, Sasmita Das, Madhusmita Nayak
pmc-13094909.description: The burden of hemiparesis on caregivers is significant, often leading to physical strain, emotional stress, social isolation, depression, and a decline in their own health. The aim is to investigate the degree of dependency of hemiparesis patients and their healthcare challenges among caregivers of stroke survivors.

pmc-13114502.title: In Vivo Microendoscopy in the Near‐Infrared II Window
pmc-13114502.creator: Zhisheng Wu, Danyang Xu, Zideng Dai, Xinyuan Wang, Wayne Jason Li, Sixin Xu, Xun Zhang, Yuanhua Liu, Puxian Xiong, Hanze Yu, Wentao Ye, Liangqiong Qu, Yongye Liang, Hongjie Dai, Feifei Wang
pmc-13114502.description: Non‐invasive fluorescence endoscopy of deep biological tissues beyond the mucosa, or trans‐intestinal imaging in live mammals with high spatiotemporal resolution, remains challenging due to light scattering. Here, we developed a near‐infrared II (NIR‐II) microendoscopy with imaging wavelength extended to 1700 nm, enabling deep intestinal imaging beyond the mucosa and transrectal imaging at sub‐10‐µm resolution without any invasive surgery.

pmc-13210345.title: Atomistic Insights into Hydrogen Diffusion and Deformation Mechanisms in FeCrNi-Based Austenitic Stainless Steels: Effects of Alloying, Temperature, and Hydrogen Concentration

pmc-13631991.title: Environmental suitability of Anopheles mosquito species in the Maekel region, Eritrea: species distribution modeling using maximum entropy
pmc-13631991.creator: Filmon Gebreyesus Mebrahtu, Kibreab Tesfamichael Haile, Adam Mengesteab Teweldebirhan, Meron Berhe Tsegai, Selam Mihreteab, Araia Berhane
pmc-13631991.description: IntroductionMalaria, a significant global health challenge, is transmitted exclusively by Anopheles mosquitoes. The dependence of mosquito habitats on environmental conditions, coupled with the established link between malaria prevalence and habitat niches, highlights the dynamic interplay between mosquito ecology and environmental factors in malaria transmission.
